verdict.reasoning: Patient states diarrhea for past three days and going to the toilet five to six times a day with watery loose stools: 'I've been having, uh, diarrhoea, for like, let's say past three days' and 'around, five to six times a day' and 'definitely watery, uh, loose stools'.

Patient describes initial vomiting and nausea which have now resolved: 'it started with vomiting, so I vomited a couple of times... but then, that went away, and, uh, yeah it's just diarrhoea now' and 'the vomiting has now stopped. Is that right? ... Yes, yes.'

No blood in stools: 'Any blood in your stools? Patient: No, not that I could see.' No abdominal pain: 'with the diarrhea have you noticed any other symptoms, like tummy pain? Patient: Uh, not, not really, no.'

Dehydration and decreased appetite/solids with weakness: 'I feel very dehydrated' and difficulty maintaining intake: 'I feel like I don't drink enough... I feel dehydrated again'; reduced solids: 'Have you managed to eat anything, solids? Patient: Uh, not much, not much... I don't really feel like, uh, I have appetite'; weakness: 'I feel very weak though.'
Subjective fever at onset, now better: 'probably at, at the beginning I was feeling I had a bit of temperature, but now I feel, I feel kind of fine.'
No headache or muscle pains: 'Any headaches or muscle pains? Patient: Not, not really, no.'

No suspect food and no known sick contacts: 'Did you have any takeaway food, or any dodgy restaurant food? Patient: Uh, not that I remember, no.' and 'Have you been around anyone unwell, with diarrhea recently...? Patient: Hmm, not that I know.'
Asthma history: 'so I, I do suffer of asthma. So, I do have my inhalers.'
Uses blue inhaler as needed: 'I do have my inhalers... I use infrequently, let's say only when I have, uh, a bit of' and doctor clarifies 'Is that the blue inhaler? ... Blue inhaler. OK, alright.'
No known drug allergies: 'Do you have any allergies to medications? Patient: Um, not that I know of.'

Father had hypertension and died of bowel cancer ~10 years ago: 'my father has, high uh, well used to have high blood pressure. He actually, so he actually died, of, bowel cancer, like ten years ago.'
Mother has type 2 diabetes: 'Ohh yes, so uh, probably is worth mentioning uh, she has diabetes.' and 'Do you know if that's type one or type two? Patient: Uh, it's type two.'
Lives alone and is a software engineer: 'Who lives at home with you, sir? Patient: Ohh I, I live alone.' and 'What's your employment? What do you do for work? Patient: I'm a software engineer.'
Off work for 3 days: 'Have you taken time off work recently? Patient: Uh, yes, yes I have, uh. Uh, these last three days I've been feeling, really unwell, so I couldn't work.'
Non-smoker and drinks socially: 'Do you do either of those? [smoking and alcohol] Patient: Uh, not really, I drink infrequently, like socially let's say, and I don't smoke.'

Doctor’s assessment and features: 'I think you're probably suffering from what we call gastroenteritis' plus prior history: 3-day watery diarrhea, initial vomiting now resolved, no blood or tummy pain, early bit of temperature now fine, feels dehydrated with reduced appetite and intake are all explicitly described earlier in the transcript.

Oral rehydration with Dioralyte: 'you can get things from the pharmacy, which is called Dioralyte, which can help replenish any uh minerals and vitamins you may have lost. ... it's a type of fluid replacement drink.'
Paracetamol for fever/weakness: 'you can take some Paracetamol if you're feeling feverish and weak.'

Off work until diarrhea-free 24–48 hours: 'I would probably advise you to continue taking time off work for next day or two' and 'normally you have to be diarrhea-free for about twenty four to forty eight hours, before you return back to work.'
Return if not improved by next week: 'Let's see how the next few days go. And if you're still not better next week, I want you to come back and see me.'
